claims.statement: packages/db-client/prisma/schema.prisma is the only persistence schema in the repo: it defines 13 tables plus six Postgres enum types, is re-exported for all consumers by packages/db-client/src/index.ts, and no component uses raw SQL ($executeRaw/$queryRaw appear nowhere in apps/), so anything the schema does not express does not exist at runtime.

The schema splits into three ownership classes: public 11e catalog tables (datasheets_11e, weapons_11e, datasheet_weapons_11e, abilities_11e, stratagems_11e, wargear_rules_11e, leader_compatibility_11e, paint_swatches) read by the unauthenticated datasheet/stratagem/weapon routes; per-user tables (user_profiles, user_armies, user_unit_media, user_color_schemes) scoped by userId in the API handlers; and sync_metadata, an ETL log written only by the sync worker and read by GET /api/changelog.

Faction, detachment and chapter identity are bare VARCHAR keys with no foreign keys — no faction or detachment table exists — so an invalid factionId or detachmentPrimary is accepted by Postgres and simply matches no rows.

Every foreign key in the schema is ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE with no RESTRICT or SET NULL anywhere: deleting a user_profiles row removes that user's armies, unit media and color schemes; deleting a user_armies row removes its user_unit_media; deleting a datasheets_11e row removes its wargear rules, abilities, weapon links and both sides of any leader_compatibility_11e row. user_unit_media has two independent cascade parents (user_id and roster_id) and abilities_11e.datasheet_id is nullable, so an ability may exist with no datasheet.

The only uniqueness constraints are weapons_11e.slug and the composite uniques on leader_compatibility_11e (leader, bodyguard), datasheet_weapons_11e (datasheet, weapon) and user_unit_media (roster_id, unit_instance_id); stratagems, abilities and paint_swatches have no unique index even though seed.ts deduplicates them by name/brand in application code, and the user_unit_media composite unique is what lets media.ts upsert a photo by (rosterId, unitInstanceId).

Five JSONB NOT NULL columns carry the unmodelled domain with no database validation at all (no CHECK, no jsonpath, no FK from inside them): UserArmy.rosterPayload, WargearRule.conditionTree, Datasheet.unitComposition, Datasheet.stats and UserColorScheme.palette.

roster_payload is persisted from req.body with only a fallback default and later cast as unknown as RosterPayload and dereferenced via rosterPayload.units.map(...), so an external token holder can store a payload without a units array and the audit route will throw inside the handler and answer 500 DB_ERROR rather than a validation error.

WargearRule.conditionTree is never read or written by application code — no reference to conditionTree exists in apps/ or packages/rules-engine-11e, and the seed inserts no wargear_rules_11e rows at all, so /api/datasheets/:id always serializes wargearRules as an empty array; likewise no application code touches user_color_schemes or paint_swatches.

user_unit_media rows are kept in step with roster_payload only by the client: PUT /api/rosters/:id replaces rosterPayload without deleting the removed unit's media row or its S3 objects, and only deleting the whole roster cascades them away.

The six Postgres enum types created by CREATE TYPE in the init migration are duplicated as string-union types in packages/types/src/index.ts, so widening a TypeScript union without an ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE migration type-checks and then fails at insert.

packages/db-client/prisma/migrations contains exactly one migration, 20261005170232_init/migration.sql (plus the postgresql migration_lock.toml), which creates all enum types, tables, indexes and foreign keys; schema evolution has never happened here, so prisma migrate deploy is a no-op after first apply.

The datasource uses the pgbouncer-style split url = env("DATABASE_URL") / directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL"); client generation runs from the root postinstall hook, but Dockerfile.api installs with npm ci --ignore-scripts and runs npx prisma generate explicitly, and wahapedia-sync.yml runs the same command as its own step, so the postinstall hook is not load-bearing.

apps/api/entrypoint.sh is the automated migration path: under set -e it defaults DIRECT_URL to DATABASE_URL so the schema's directUrl validates on plain Postgres, runs npx prisma migrate deploy, and only then execs the API — so a failing pending migration aborts the container before node starts. With DATABASE_URL unset it logs 'catalog-only mode', skips migrations and boots anyway. Dockerfile.api copies the prisma directory and the prisma/@prisma packages into the runtime stage solely to support this.

packages/db-client/prisma/seed.ts (run via tsx, registered as the prisma.seed hook and exposed as npm run db:seed) is re-runnable but protected three different ways: findFirst-then-create guards for stratagems, paint swatches and abilities (best-effort, with no unique index behind them); upsert on the real unique slug for weapons and on composite uniques for the link tables; and upsert on hard-coded UUIDs with an empty update object for the five datasheets.

Because the datasheet upserts pass update: {} against hard-coded fixture UUIDs (11111111-...0001-0003, 22222222-...0001-0002), editing a seeded datasheet in seed.ts will not propagate to a database that already holds the row; the row must be deleted (cascading to its rules, abilities and links) or edited directly.

seed.ts writes only catalog tables: it creates no user_profiles, wargear_rules_11e or sync_metadata rows. Since user_armies.user_id has a FK to user_profiles(id) and no code path in the repo inserts a profile, a roster write for an unknown JWT sub is rejected by the FK and surfaces as 500 DB_ERROR.

In the dev stack, migrations plus seed are applied by the one-shot db-init service running scripts/dev-container.sh db: it waits for Postgres, runs prisma migrate deploy, then npx tsx packages/db-client/prisma/seed.ts with a non-zero seed exit logged and swallowed ('seed is idempotent fallback data'), then idles with tail -f /dev/null so logs stay readable; it re-runs on every up.

In the pull-based prod composition the api service receives DATABASE_URL but no DIRECT_URL, relying entirely on the entrypoint's DIRECT_URL default; sync-worker is the only prod service given DIRECT_URL explicitly, and its fallback password differs from DATABASE_URL's (${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres} vs :-postgrespassword) — harmless only because the worker image ships no schema and runs no migrations.

packages/db-client/prisma/rls-policies.sql is intent, not enforcement: it enables RLS and creates auth.uid() = user_id policies on user_armies, user_unit_media and user_color_schemes, but no migration or script applies it, auth.uid() is a Supabase function absent from plain Postgres, the compose DSNs are the postgres superuser which bypasses RLS anyway, and user_profiles is covered by no policy at all.

The Wahapedia ETL never mutates catalog rows: per endpoint per pass it reads the newest sync_metadata row, sends If-None-Match, compares a SHA-256 content hash, and inserts one new row with status NO_DELTA, SUCCESS or ERROR plus recordCount and a date-derived rulesetVersionId (11.1.0-YYYY-QN-MFM), making sync_metadata an append-only audit log indexed on (endpoint, syncedAt) rather than per-endpoint state.

The ruleset version id exists only as independent string literals: GET /api/changelog derives it from the newest sync_metadata row and falls back to '11.1.0-2026-Q3-MFM' when the table is empty, POST /api/rosters hard-codes user_armies.ruleset_version_id to '11.1.0-2026-Q3', and the sync worker regenerates it from the current date — no constraint ties them together.

updated_at columns are maintained by Prisma's @updatedAt, not by the database — there is no trigger or default — so any future raw-SQL or manual UPDATE leaves them stale, and the catalog tables (datasheets_11e, weapons_11e, abilities_11e, stratagems_11e, wargear_rules_11e, paint_swatches, sync_metadata) have no updated_at column at all, modelling them as insert-only.

The authoritative table count is 13: the init migration contains exactly 13 CREATE TABLE statements and schema.prisma declares 13 models, while docs/DEPLOYMENT.md contradicts itself — §3.1 claims a fresh self-migrated database has 14 tables and §3.2 says 13 — so the §3.1 figure is a documentation bug, not a 14th modelled table.

The prod composition's api service pulls the published image with no command override, so a fresh production or CI database is migrated to the full schema by the image entrypoint's prisma migrate deploy — Docker on the host is the only requirement, with no source checkout, Node install or Prisma CLI — which is why Dockerfile.api must copy packages/db-client/prisma plus the prisma/@prisma packages into its runtime stage, while the sync-worker runtime stage carries only built dist output and therefore cannot migrate at all.

Unset variables in docker-compose.prod.yml fall back to the public placeholder credentials postgres/postgrespassword on database forceorg_dev — the same DSN .env.example and the dev/source-build compositions hard-code — so a zero-config test stack boots and self-migrates the schema the documented commands assume; seeding stays a separate manual host step because no prod service or image runs seed.ts, leaving a fresh prod catalog empty until someone runs it (or a sync pass).
